Counter Strike and Diablo were fucking nice when I was a kid, but games like Halo have a special place in my heart because of the memories I have of playing with my little brother. What happened to couch co-op? Why is it that modern games don't seem to support it anymore?

The motivation is money. Video game developers push for multiplayer online gaming because there is more money in it. But couch co-op is a lot of fun. TVs are so huge these days. There's definitely enough 'real estate' to make a good local multiplayer experience.
It's harder to render iirc. Since relatively few people use it they'd rather put that hardware power toward better graphics.

You can sell more copies of the game if you require each player in a multi-player game to have their own copy on their own system.

That said, local multi-player games still come out. Sportsfriends gets very good reviews, for example. But they're rarer.

Money plan and simple. Yeah it's hard to render both screens but the N64 and PS had split screen games. It's safe to say our computing power has gotten a bit better since then. If devs don't have to spend time working on a split screen mode and instead just make people buy a second copy then the business answer is obvious.

It's a smaller demographic, so most companies cut it out to aim at the majority. Nintendo is a holdout in this area, and Diablo 3 has pretty well implemented couch co-op. If you're interested in couch co-op or just co-op in general, check out Voat's co-op gaming sub, /v/CoOpGaming
